reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20-30 feet over trees with minnows.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: The bite is picking up, with two bass over 9 pounds checked in this week. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide
reports.by: Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: It was a warm rain that pushed a lot of bait shallow, consequently bass and white bass should be up there shallow with them in the creeks. Crappie are loaded in main ditches and creek channel timber and brush.
reports.by: Cade Rudiger, local angler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding on shad and bluegill gearing up for winter. Crappie are schooled up on main lake brush piles and deep grass lines hitting crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water working moving baits and plastics over and around the grass. There are plenty of bass suspended around bait balls in 10-25 feet of water, so cast small swimbaits and flukes above.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on rocks and ledges with a shaky head or crankbait. A frog or wakebait around grass will catch some good bass as well.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: There is good bass top water action with choppos or spook type baits early around pond weed or grass. Crappie are good in deep trees in 15-30 feet of water suspended in 15-22 feet.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Water stained; 79 degrees; Fishing has been slow overall, with redfish, black bass, stripers, and shadow cats all showing limited activity.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Post cold front the crappie will either push shallow or go deep, and hybrids and white bass will be slower. Crappie are good on the docks, and brush piles in 15-30 feet with minnows, or natural colored jigs. Largemouth bass are good using topwaters, flukes, senkos, and chatterbaits on main lake rock and around docks. White bass and hybrids are scattered on main lake humps and points with topwaters, slabs or trolling. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 4.96 pounds are excellent in 3-8 feet of water on wake baits Hag’s green pumpkin tornados along shoreline grass with chatterbaits, crankbaits and jigs in the brush 5-12 feet of water. Crappie are excellent to 15 inches on minnows and jigs on main lake scattered brush piles in 12-20 feet of water. White bass are slow to 1.50 pounds on crappie jigs and crankbaits out of the lights at night and schooling action in the open water of the main lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught with topwater baits, or on ledges with Carolina rigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with fish piled up on rocks and ledges in and around creek mouths.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The bass are still in a transitional stage as we go from hot to cooler temperatures. The white bass and crappie should pick up as the weather cools and there is some current.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Black bass and stripers are slow at the moment, and the water level is about one foot below normal.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: There is an early morning largemouth bass topwater bite with small walking baits or poppers. Smallmouth bass have also been very active around these areas with finesse jigs, ned rigs or small creature baits on a light Texas rig.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Productive setups include slabs, spinnerbaits, and Alabama rigs, especially when using the sawtooth retrieve technique.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank anglers are reporting good action on black bass, white bass, and crappie, with excellent catches of catfish and channel catfish as well.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass action is tremendous with many folks bragging on 100 plus fish per day.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting well around grass beds and docks on creature baits and are also hitting crankbaits on wind-blown points and near shad schools. Crappie are being caught on structure in 12-19 feet of water, mostly on hair jigs and minnows, with some smaller fish mixed in. Hybrid and white bass are scattered and schooling flats and along drop-offs in 12-22 feet, hitting slabs, spoons, and shad.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs and minnows around boat dock and over deep water brush piles. Black bass are fair on swimbaits and spinnerbaits in 4-6 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in 12-15 feet of water with shaky heads or dropshots.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite is good with topwaters, buzz baits popper, and sexy dawgs on points and around grass. Black Bass are beginning to school in open water. Cooler nights will drop water temperatures and bass will move shallower. Streamers are enticing bass early and late. Crappie are good as the fish transition to a fall and winter pattern. Small hand tied jigs actually out fished minnows this week on my boat but any crappie baits will get you bit as water temps cool down.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good offshore in 8-15 feet of water. Bass are in the grass, but it can be difficult to find good areas of grass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 12-14 feet of water on brush with minnows. Bass are good in the pockets with moving baits. Bass are feeding on schools of shad early and late in the day.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are good to excellent mid-lake near Bentwater on slabs and spinnerbaits. Largemouth bass are good in numbers and many are schooling with the sand bass on flats adjacent to the deeper channels. Crappie action continues to be good to excellent on small jigs or minnows fished on submerged structure, standing timber or bridge pilings.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Continue to look for working birds and target fish jigging slabs in 15-17 feet of water.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are active with the cooler weather, biting well on spinnerbaits, crankbaits, and chatterbaits, while grubs on a light Texas rig in green or crawfish-red are also producing. Crappie fishing is fair to great in the East Fork and Lucious Bayou, holding 10-12 feet deep near structure, though the rain may have moved some fish out of the channels. White bass are schooling on humps on the south end and hitting slabs, swimbaits, and trolled baits, especially early and late in the day.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting soft plastics on brush and offshore structure at any depth up to 25 feet. A few bass can be caught on topwater walking baits, buzz baits, poppers and ploppers.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair schooling on timber in the flats off the river channel with 2 inch plastics jigs. Bass are still being caught in shallow water around shoreline cover and creek swings. As cooler weather continues, bass will begin transitioning toward major creek channels and secondary points. Crappie remain consistent on standing timber in 15–20 feet of water, with fish holding 8–12 feet down.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be caught on brush and standing timber in 10-20 feet with minnows and jigs. The best bite is on white or chartreuse 1 ounce slabs.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, spoons, spinnerbaits and live bait are working. Crappie are fair in 10-28 feet of water. Largemouth are sitting around shallow rocks and brush pretty well through the day.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Bass anglers should focus on wind-blown points and coves, where reaction baits like spinnerbaits, chatterbaits, and shallow crankbaits are producing before the front fully settles in.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Look for early morning bass topwater action.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good using flukes and senkos over the hydrilla. Crappie have slowed and scattered. Sand bass are excellent on slab spoons at the east side of Dirgin bridge and in mid lake flats in 20 feet.
reports.by: Hambone fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good working topwater baits sub surface quickly, or using Carolina rigs off points in 12-15 feet of water. Crappie are fair for 9-12 inch fish on brush piles, with fish 14 inches or larger in the standing field above the power lines.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing remains good, while catfish have been slow. Largemouth are excellent on topwater frogs shallow near grass. Black crappie are excellent with small white crappie jigs over brush piles.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slower than normal, but still finding several on brush.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 8 pounds on vibrating jigs, frogs and the new Hags flatliner worm. Crappie are slowing down with few limits reported but they are still biting on minnows and jigs and shad colors suspended in trees 8-12 feet.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on timber in 10-24 feet of water on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on topwater poppers, or Carolina rigs off secondary points. Black crappie are excellent on brush piles. White crappie are roaming in deeper water but are more difficult to catch.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Good numbers of fish with flutter spoons and slabs after the surface schooling stopped. Crappie bite continues to improve targeting tree tops at 15-30 feet on minnows and jigs. Casting under docks is producing catches of crappie. Largemouth bass fishing has been slower this week, but should start picking up as the water cools off. Lots of undersized smallmouth bass are being caught on the south end of the lake on crankbaits near the rock points.
reports.by: Captain Casey Armstrong, Hooked Up Outfitters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Four largemouth bass, ranging from 2-5 pounds, were caught from the bank using topwater popping frogs and crankbaits.
reports.by: Aric Brooks, Huntsville State Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass can be caught covering water with Biffle Bugs, chatterBaits and squarebill crankbaits. After the midweek cold front the 309 flats and the Pelican Island area should be good areas to target hybrids and white bass with slabs in 20-25 feet.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Fish main lake points in 8-15 feet using inline spinners and slab spoons. Crappie are improving under bridges and on shallow brush with the bite on minnows. Largemouth bass are extremely shallow and prefer fast moving shallow crankbaits and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Bass and crappie action has tapered off, and with the lake elevation at 39.91 feet, conditions are expected to worsen as a cold front moves in.
reports.by: Chad Kinsfather, Lavaca Navidad River Authority

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are piled up on brush in 12-18 feet of water. Stripers are good with slabs in 10-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: The lake is fishing well overall, and bass can be caught from shallow to deep water. No new crappie reports this week, though a few anglers mentioned the bite has been slow.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with water temperatures in the high 70s and water clarity as good as a couple feet on the lower end of the lake. With the water temps dropping, the shad are starting to move into coves and the bass are following.
reports.by: Tyler Torwick, Torwick's Guiding Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows 16-20 feet of water on brush piles. Bass are fair on trick worms, spinnerbaits and crankbaits.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie feed heavily the days leading into a cold front. Before the cold front this week crappie were excellent on structure in 15-20 feet of water with any color and size of artificials, or with dead or live minnows. A 6 pound black bass was caught mixed in with the crappie on a brush pile. Once the water reaches around 65 degrees the crappie will push to deeper water. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow around docks with crankbaits. Crappie are fair on brush piles with minnows and jigs. After the cold front crappie should start showing in the crappie house.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great in shallow water using crankbaits with big vibration. Crappie are good using minnows in timber. Sand bass are excellent with large schools early in the morning on slabs and fast moving baits.
reports.by: Michael James, local angler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow with fish sitting on the edges of the main river channel on structure in 14-21 feet of water on hair jigs tipped with minnows.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 18-29 feet over trees with minnows.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding on shad off main lake points and flats. When you can find bass use a topwater or a spoon. Crappie are schooled up on main lake brush piles and deep grass lines in 12-20 feet of water hitting crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting in open water and around vegetation.
reports.by: Ander Meine, Bassquatch Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 18-30 feet of water on small minnows near trees and stumps.
reports.by: Hundley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass bite is good with topwaters like poppers, frogs and buzz baits around pond weed 1-4 feet of water. Some schooling bass are popping up in the flats. Crappie are good in deep trees in 15-30 feet of water suspended in 15-22 feet.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Redfish are sluggish in 510 feet of water, and channel catfish, stripers, and black bass are also slow to bite.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8.64 pounds are excellent in 3-8 feet of water on buzz baits and topwater frogs in the shoreline grass, and on chatterbaits, crankbaits and jigs in the brush 5-12 feet of water. Crappie are excellent with catches up to 12 inches on minnows and jigs on the main lake scattered brush piles in 12-20 feet of water. White bass are slow to 1.50 pounds on crappie jigs and crankbaits out of the lights at night, with some schooling action in open water on the main lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The bass are hunkered down in a transitional mode with the cold mornings and hot afternoons, they do not know if it is November or August.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Black bass and stripers remain slow, with limited activity reported.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: As the nights become cooler the water temperature is slowly declining bringing bass into shallow water. The morning bass bite has been solid on a spook and chatterbait.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Productive setups include slabs, spinners, and A-rigs, especially when using the sawtooth retrieve technique.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are finding excellent action for white bass and crappie from the bank, along with good catches of channel and blue catfish.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass action is improving on wind-blown points, docks, and offshore structure in 2-20 feet of water. Crappie are being found around structure and timber in 12-20 feet, with many juveniles caught; hair jigs are producing best, though minnows and plastics are also working. Hybrid and white bass are schooling in smaller groups on flats and drop-offs in 14-21 feet, biting slabs, spoons, and shad.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair around boat docks on minnows and jigs. White bass are good to fair on slabs and rattle traps. Black bass are fair on swimbaits and spinnerbaits in 4-6 feet of water early then the bite slows down by mid morning.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Target clean pockets of water for bass with shaky heads, underspins or dropshots.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass bite is good until the sun rises. Black Bass are beginning to school in open water. Cooler nights will drop water temperatures and bass will move shallower. Streamers are enticing bass early and late. Lake Fork crappie fishing is getting better and better as we head into fall. Black crappie are loading up at the base of trees, some brush piles, underwater bridges and we should see them on bridges soon. White crappie are loading up on trees and brush piles in 13-32 feet and should be moving towards the dam and deeper water soon. We have had good luck with larger minnows threaded onto 1/16 ounce jig heads for white crappie on timber.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Big Country Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Target bass is shallow water with cover and structure using topwaters, chatterbaits and weightless worms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 12-14 feet of water on brush with minows. Bass are good in the pockets with moving baits. Bass are feeding on schools of shad early and late in the day.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Lots of anglers are catching sand bass on spinnerbaits and slabs mid lake. Largemouth bass numbers are good with an occasional bigger fish mixed in. Some early morning topwater action is occurring and many of the largemouth are schooling with the sandbass. Crappie action continues to be good to excellent on small minnows and jigs worked near submerged structures. Best crappie reports are from in town to near Indian Harbor.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Target fish jigging slabs in 15-17 feet of water.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: White bass are schooling heavily on humps in 12-14 feet of water on the south end and can be caught trolling deep jet divers with gold pet spoons or by vertical jigging with Duck Tracker slabs. Largemouth bass, mostly in the 2-3 pound range, are hitting crankbaits, spinnerbaits, and grubs around cypress tree knobs in 3-4 feet of water. Crappie are aggressive and biting great near brush piles in 10-12 feet, especially in Lucious Bayou, the East Fork, and West Fork side lakes.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting soft plastics on docks, and shallow or deep brush. Schooling bass can be caught on wacky worms, topwaters, and swimbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 12-20 feet of water at the base of trees off creek channels and main channel, or in ditches off the main channel using 1/16 ounce hair jigs. Bass activity has been productive during early morning hours with topwater presentations. As the day progresses, bass are transitioning to deeper ambush points. Crappie fishing remains consistent across the lake.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 15-20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are moving shallow hitting topwater frogs and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 6-18 feet of water on offshore brush, standing timber and concrete. Largemouth bass are in 4-12 feet of water on brush, docks and bulkheads hitting Texas rigs and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is heating up and should remain solid in the coming weeks, while white bass are being caught in the main lake, upper river, and below the dam. Largemouth bass up to 7-pounds are hitting medium-diving crankbaits off main lake rocky points and riprap, as well as Charlie’s Flippin Bugs on shaky heads around mid and lower-lake boathouses. Crappie are steady in the Riverside area and major creeks like Bethy, White Rock, and Harmon, hitting minnows and black-and-chartreuse tube jigs near log jams and laydowns about 6 feet down. White bass action is improving in the upper river channel and mid-lake humps in 12-19 feet, with whites and occasional stripers hitting slabs, crankbaits…

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with chatterbaits, lipless crankbaits and weightless senkos over the hydrilla. Crappie are fair around brush piles in 18-28 feet on minnows. Sand bass are in 20 feet of water hitting small slab spoons.
reports.by: Hambone Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth and sand bass have been caught everywhere this week. Some nice largemouth bass and white bass have been caught on glass colored rapala with red stripes, whopper popper lures and minnows. Smallmouth bass have been great using gold panther spinnerbaits. Crappie are slow around the Sanford Yake Dock, Blue West, and Bugbee.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-5 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Bass are holding back in the shade around heavy cover to escape the sunlight. Early morning and late evening topwater is also effective for targeting bass. Baitfish are beginning to transition into the backs of pockets and upriver with the bass close behind. Crappie are fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 6 pounds. Bass are best on topwaters, or walking baits early around dead salt cedar in pockets with 5 feet of water or less. Crappie are good with reports of limits.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: When you can locate crappie or white bass the bite is best on minnows. Black bass are slow.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Two 4-pound largemouth bass were caught on swimbaits along with several smaller 1-2 pound bass taken on Ridge Lizards and Palmetto Bugz. With the cooler weather, crappie are likely still biting - many anglers have been fishing from the piers this past week, and it appears crappie are what they’re after.
reports.by: Aric Brooks, Huntsville State Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 20-28 feet of water, or timber in 6-8 or 12-18 feet of water. Largemouth bass are good with buzz baits and topwater lures. Sand bass are fair on humps with live bait, or slabs. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: There are more crappie on brush piles now, they have been difficult to find in large numbers for a while. Black bass can be caught on docks with chattrtbaits and squarebill crankbaits.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the marina the crappie bite is slow, bluegill are fair on crickets or worms, and catfish are good on minnows and punch baits. Crappie are fair on various jigs and minnows in 6-12 feet of water over mainlake brush. Black bass are slow on craw jigs and slowly working plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Unseasonably warm conditions have bass holding in a summer pattern.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are active in brush in 8-15 feet of water using jigs and minnows. Look for largemouth and smallmouth bass to be active in the backs of coves and creek channels early and late in the day.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Out deeper, big crankbaits and Carolina rigs are producing on main lake points and ridges in 18-22 feet - look for shad, as bass are starting to follow the bait. Crappie fishing should improve some but will depend on how much rain falls this week, as the bite remains a bit slow for now.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are improving due to the cooler evening temperatures, but the most consistent fishing still has been deep. Bass are biting small paddle tail swimbaits fished around brushy shorelines with a 45-degree slope, along with drop-shot rigged finesse worms.
reports.by: Tyler Torwick, Torwick's Guiding Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs in 8-12 feet of water, and on brush piles in 25 feet. Bass are slow on trick worms, spinnerbaits and crankbaits.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Before the recent cold front the big crappie were aggressively feeding live bait or artificials in 10-15 feet of water on structures. Crappie bite should be fair to good heading into the weekend. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Thick mats of hydrilla throughout the coves and flats have create difficult fishing conditions for bass.
reports.by: Team YAKUSA

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is excellent up against cattails and in shallow water with topwaters and jerkbaits. Crappie fishing is good around bridge pylons using minnows. Slabs and jigs are working best.
reports.by: Michael James, local angler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 12-20 feet of water at the base of trees off creek channels and main channel, or in ditches off the main channel using 1/16 ounce hair jigs.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has improved in the shallows, especially around newly flooded vegetation using buzzbaits and flipping plastics. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide
reports.by: Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are holding around submerged vegetation in 12 feet or more of water, biting best on drop-shot rigged finesse worms and light Texas-rigged stick worms.
reports.by: Ander Meine, Bassquatch Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with buzz baits, topwater frogs, choppos and poppers early around pond weed. Bass are good on Texas rigs, but best on creature baits around big timber and bushes on flats 7-12 feet. Crappie are good in deep trees in 15-30 feet of water suspended in 15-22 feet.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Black bass, stripers, and catfish remain slow, with limited action reported across the lake.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Striper and black bass have been slow, with limited activity reported this week.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are schooling around submerged hydrilla.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Water temperature is around 85 degrees, and bank fishing has been excellent all over, with good catches of black bass, crappie, and both channel and blue catfish.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good to excellent on Texas rigged worms and shallow crankbaits on the upper ends.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass reports are strong, with good fish on edges at first light and under docks or offshore structures during the day; poppers and shallow-running baits work early, switching to Ol’ Monster Plum midday. Crappie are being found on structure and timber in 12-20 feet, mostly juveniles, with minnows, hair jigs, or plastics working best. Hybrid and white bass are schooling on flats and drop-off edges in 14-21 feet, hitting slabs, spoons, and shad, with some smaller schools mixed in; check the tooth patch via the Outdoor Annual app to distinguish hybrids from whites.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on swimbaits. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows around boat docks and over brush. Sand bass are good on slabs in deep water over humps.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Some bass can be caught early in front of reeds or over grass with rattle traps, and underspins.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Big Country Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Lots of anglers are catching sand bass on spinnerbaits and slabs mid lake. Largemouth bass numbers are good with an occasional bigger fish mixed in. Some early morning topwater action is occurring and many of the largemouth are schooling with the sandbass. Best action for Blues are in town to near Hunter Park.Crappie action continues to be good to excellent on small minnows and jigs worked near submerged structures. Best crappie reports are from in town to near Indian Harbor.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Water clarity on the south end of Lake Houston is around 1.5-2 feet, with light flow throughout the lake creating good conditions for largemouth bass fishing. Bass are hitting early and late around riprap and rocky areas on deep or shallow-diving crankbaits and spinnerbaits, then moving to deeper points and submerged structures as the sun rises, where grubs, Texas-rigged worms, and swimbaits are productive. Crappie fishing is excellent in river channels 10-14 feet deep, especially near structure; live minnows or hand-tied jigs are working best in murkier areas like East Fork and Lucious Bayou. White bass are schooling on the south end around humps in 12-14 feet, biting slabs and trolled…
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 10-20 feet on brush timber and standing timber with minnows and jigs. The best bite is on white or chartreuse 1 ounce slabs.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are best targeted on structure using Carolina-rigged worms, and the occasional topwater or schooling bass shows up on reaction baits. Crappie are fair to good around brush piles and submerged timber, particularly using minnows and jigs. White bass dominate the lake’s reputation - schools are active, especially in the lower parts of the lake, and slabs, spoons, or trolling tactics are effective.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good along the hydrilla with senkos and offshore brush piles with deep crankbaits. Crappie are excellent, fish are suspended in timber and brush in 20-25 feet. Sand bass are good on small hair jigs and small slab spoons in 15-20 feet.
reports.by: Hambone Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth and sand bass have been caught everywhere this week. Some nice largemouth, and white bass have been caught on red and white crank baits, whopper popper lures and minnows. Crappie have been slow again around the Sanford Yake Dock, North Canyon, and Fritch Fortress.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on Carolina rigged flukes, and Texas rig ribbon tails on deep creek channel swings. Bass are in nice size schools in 12-15 feet of water. Bass are good on bottom baits and deep diving crankbaits. Crappie are excellent in the standing timber, with quality fish and numbers possible. Crappie are in brush piles and secondary points in 12 feet of water, with big ones isolated in 20-25 feet.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie remains good, while catfish have been slow. Largemouth bass are excellent on a Carolina rig on a secondary point and 12-15 feet, but fish are primarily schooling. Crappie are excellent with white and chartreuse lightweight jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are staying strong and consistent off brush piles in the lake. Still a few largemouth bass being caught off minnows from the banks.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow to 7 pounds on topwater frogs early in the morning. Crappie are fair suspended 8-12 feet down around hardwood trees.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on topwater, poppers, small walking baits as well as flukes. Crappie are fair with a white crappie jig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Good numbers of fish with flutter spoons and slabs after the surface schooling stopped. Crappie bite continues to improve targeting tree tops at 15-30 feet on minnows and jigs. Casting under docks is producing numbers of crappie. Largemouth bass fishing has been slower this week, but should start picking up as the water cools off. Lots of undersized smallmouth bass are being caught on the south end of the lake on crankbaits near the rock points.
reports.by: Captain Casey Armstrong, Hooked Up Outfitters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Not much to report this week, but a group of anglers were catching crappie off the fishing piers using live minnows under bobbers, so it sounds like the crappie bite is picking up right now.
reports.by: Aric Brooks, Huntsville State Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are going to continue on a boat dock pattern in the major creek arms.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: As a bonus, schooling largemouth bass, generally less than 15 inches, are very predictably feeding in open water on the surface as they trap shad there. Larger bass are coming from submerged vegetation in 12–20 feet of water on drop-shot rigged finesse worms. For better numbers, target nomadic schools of open-water bass chasing shad.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Catfishing is good, while crappie are fair in the north section of the lake.
reports.by: Chad Kinsfather, Lavaca Navidad River Authority

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Small slabs in 8-15 feet of water on shallow flats for small stripers and sandbass. Crappie are on the brush piles and in docks in 12-18 feet of water with jigs. Bigger crappie are roaming near creeks and stumpy flats. Largemouth bass and smallmouth bass are off the banks on brush in 8-12 feet of water. The best fish can be caught early on topwaters, then take the topwater to deeper water switching to slabs as the sun rises.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are improving due to the cooler evening temperatures, but the most consistent fishing still has been deep. Bass are biting along 45-degree sloping shorelines with a mix of rock, brush, and docks, mostly in less than 15 feet of water.
reports.by: Tyler Torwick, Torwick's Guiding Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs in 8-12 feet of water, and on brush piles in 25 feet. Bass are fair on trick worms, spinnerbaits and crankbaits.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow around docks with crankbaits. Crappie are slow on brush piles with minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing are good against any structure in shallow water. Crappie fair around bridge columns with minnows. Sand bass are chasing schools of bait on the deep end of the lake hitting slabs.
reports.by: Michael James, local angler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 15-20 feet over brush.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Aquilla fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 15-20 feet of water on minnows and jigs. Bass are good on spinnerbaits in 3-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great schooling midlake.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent from 10-25 feet of water in the river channels.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with buzz baits, topwater frogs, choppos and poppers early around pond weed. Bass are good on Texas rigs, but best on creature baits around big timber and bushes on flats 7-12 feet. Crappie are excellent on breaklines in 15-25 feet of water, or creek channels leading out of coves. Some crappie are starting to school up and roam, but a majority of fish are still related to structure. Crappie are thickening up so quality fish can be caught to fill the freezer.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow to 2.67 pounds. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, black bass, and stripers are also slow.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on the docks, and brush piles in 15-30 feet with minnows, or natural colored jigs. Largemouth bass are good using topwaters, flukes, senkos, and chatterbaits on main lake rock and around docks. White bass and hybrids are scattered on main lake humps and points with topwaters, slabs or trolling. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 7.69 pounds are good in 3-8 feet of water on topwater frogs in the shoreline grass with some fish on flukes, chatterbaits, crankbaits and jigs in the brush 5-12 feet. Crappie are excellent to 13 inches on minnows and jigs on the main lake scattered brush piles in 10-20 feet of water. White bass are slow to 1.50 pounds on crappie jigs and crankbaits out of the lights at night and schooling action in the open water of the main lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The bass are schooling all over the lake and in the river and bayou systems. You can catch bass on the lake with a fluke, chatterbait, swimbait or frogs. Some bass relating to lily pads and grass can be caught on topwater frogs, or punching if you want to power fish the jungle.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is slowly improving. Bass are also starting to work their way into the brush along the banks with the cooler nights.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and white bass fishing are excellent right now, with black bass rated fair.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are also abundant and anglers boast of numerous catches up to 7 pounds.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are hitting early along the edges and later on offshore structures up to 20 feet deep, with plum colored Ol’ Monster worms producing best. Crappie fishing has slowed this week but they’re still being found around structure and timber in 12-20 feet of water, mostly smaller fish, biting on minnows, hair jigs, and plastics - once the bite slows, try relocating. Hybrid and white bass are schooling on flats and drop-offs in 14-21 feet, hitting slabs, spoons, and shad.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with some fish still shallow in 2-6 feet of water at the base of trees, and some fish have transitioned to the creek channels in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are primarily on structure, but a few are transitioning to roam in creek channels.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Not much has changed this week, with bass still biting well on rocky points and ledges.
reports.by: Jimmy Steed, Lake Falcon Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow while the lake is stained from a possible turnover, and the super moon. Small bait fish are along the bank early in the morning bringing some small 4-5 inch bass shallow. Bass are slow early in the morning working underspins on points just off the grass, then rattletraps and deep diving crankbaits off the bank.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with yellow magic and buzzbait topwaters around grass, and rage swimmers around grass in 1-4 feet of water. Bass are fair with deep crankbaits in 22-25 feet on long points. Black Bass are beginning to school in open water. Cooler nights will drop water temperatures and bass will move shallower. Streamers are enticing bass early and late. Lake Fork crappie fishing is getting better and better as we head into fall. Black crappie are loading up at the base of trees, some brush piles, underwater bridges and we should see them on bridges soon. White crappie are loading up on trees and brush piles in 13-32 feet and should be moving towards the dam and deeper water soon. We have had…
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush with minnows and jigs. Black bass to 2.69 pounds are slow in 3-8 feet of water on shad or crawfish colored crankbaits and jigs in the brush 5-12 feet of water. Crappie are slow to 13 inches on minnows and jigs on the main lake scattered brush piles in 10-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Big Country Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with minnows in 12-14 feet on main lake brush. Bass are shallow schooling on shad in pockets.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie action continues to be good on structure on many areas of the lake. Sand bass action is good midlake on spinnerbait and slabs. Many of the largemouth bass are also schooling with the sand bass. Bigger largemouth bass are good near deeper docks, near creek entrances, and main lake points. Best baits for largemouth bass include topwaters early and crankbaits or soft plastics later.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on plastic worms fished in shallow cover all over the lake. Crappie are good on jigs and minnows fished over cover in 4-15 feet of water. White bass are good on slab spoons fished over points and main lake ridges.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good along the south bank casting slab spoons under the birds.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Captain King Sire reports excellent crappie action on Lake Houston, with fish holding tight to structure in 8-14 feet of water and biting well on jigs and minnows near the main river channel and drop-offs with light current. Largemouth bass are hitting strong in the shallows early around cypress trees and stumps on grubs, spinnerbaits, and crankbaits, then moving to docks and deeper drop-offs later in the day for Texas-rigged worms.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good around docks in 8–14 feet of water on a dropshot rigged finesse worms.
reports.by: Ander Meine, Bassquatch Fishing,

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on deeper brush with jigs and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on flats off the river channel in 15-22 feet of water with 2 inch crappie jigs.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing has slowed to fair in 15-20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good with a white spinnerbaits in the mornings around shallow structure. Crappie bite has been fair in brush piles around 18 feet of water.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good off points on Carolina rigged worms and Texas rigs. Crappie are good suspended over brush piles in 20-25 feet of water using Bobby Garland jigs and minnows. Small slab spoons work well bouncing off the bottom.
reports.by: Hambone fishingReport by Hambone Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good dragging small Carolina rigged soft plastics along the bottom of main lake points in 12-15 feet of water. There are numbers of bass midlake that can be found with forward facing sonar. Crappie are good with smaller fish on brush and bigger fish isolated in small groups in timber or creeks above the powerlines.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie remains good, while catfish have been slow. Largemouth bass are good dragging small Carolina rigged soft plastics along the bottom of main lake points in 12-15 feet of water. There are numbers of bass midlake that can be found with forward facing sonar. Crappie are excellent on the deep brush piles and flooded timber with crappie jigs on a light line.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good around deep brush piles and boat docks with minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good dragging small Carolina rigged soft plastics along the bottom of main lake points in 12-15 feet of water. There are numbers of bass midlake that can be found with forward facing sonar. Crappie are slow with a white 1/32 ounce crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: The only notable reports are of two 2-pounders and 1 3-pound largemouth bass caught a few days ago on Texas-rigged Zoom Ol’ Monster worms in plum and red colors.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush piles in 12-15 feet of water, or bridge columns.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 20-28 feet of water, or timber in 9-14 feet of water. Use live minnows or natural bait colored jigs Largemouth bass can be caught on offshore rocks in 16-22 feet of water with black and blue jigs, or shallow vegetation that is matting up in 4-8 feet of water with spinnerbaits, chatterbaits, or swimbaits. Dan's Crappie Co.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: As a bonus, schooling largemouth bass, generally less than 15 inches, are very predictably feeding in open water on the surface as they trap shad there.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Fish main lake points in 8-15 feet using inline spinners and slab spoons. Crappie are improving under bridges and on shallow brush with the bite on minnows. Largemouth bass are extremely shallow and preferring fast moving shallow crankbaits and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Swimbaits and slabs are still producing whites and stripers. Crappie are starting to fire up on the brush piles and in docks. The best fish can be caught early on topwaters, then take the topwater to deeper water switching to slabs as the sun rises.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite on Lake Travis has been good in the mornings, but with the heat has been slower midday. Bass are following shad into the mouths of creeks and coves. Bass are also feeding on flats and shallow ledges around larger boulders.
reports.by: Tyler Torwick, Torwick's Guiding Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs in 16-20 feet of water on brush piles. Bass are fair on trick worms, spinnerbaits and crankbaits.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good to excellent on live bait and purple and chartreuse ⅛ ounce artificials in 10-20 feet of water on brush or structure. Black bass up to 6 pounds are good on topwaters in the early morning, or deep diving crankbaits on ledges. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow around docks with crankbaits. Crappie are fair on brush piles with minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the main lake brush in 15-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass are good using soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water early in the morning on shallow running crankbaits and topwater lures. Crappie are good under bridges using minnows. The best bite is on slabs.
reports.by: Michael James, local angler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in the timber outside the creek channels and the sides of the river channel in 12-18 feet of water with hair jigs tipped minnows. Bass can be caught on main lake points with swimbaits.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be fair in 20 feet of water using minnows.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Bass anglers are finding success either shallow out to 5 feet of water, or deeper in 25 feet or more. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide
reports.by: Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good moving to shallow water to feed on shad. Crappie are great congregated in big schools around brush, timber, and in the channels.
reports.by: Cade Rudiger, local angler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to feed on shad off main lake points and flats. When you can find bass use a topwater or a spoon. Crappie are schooled up on main lake brush piles and deep grass lines in 12-20 feet of water hitting crappie jigs or minnows.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding up good on Lake Austin. There is a good shallow bite while bass are feeding on bait fish. Some nice bass in the 3-5 pound range can be caught in the grass with flukes, wacky worms, frogs, dropshots and punching rigs. Bass are great schooling midlake.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with small topwaters, frogs and jerkbaits will get some bites as well as a shaky head with a finesse or trick worm. Look for some bass schooling up after shad.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on live minnows in 18-30 feet on brush piles and timber.
reports.by: Hundley's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie will start staging in deep water or creeks and river channels. Crappie are good in timber, brush and around docks with jigs or minnows.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good as fish transition to deeper water to a fall pattern, but can still be shallow.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Redfish are fair in 15-20 feet of water, while black bass and catfish action remains slow.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on the docks, and brush piles in 15-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair using topwaters, crankbaits, and chatterbaits on main lake rock and around docks. White bass and hybrids are scattered on main lake humps and points with topwaters, slabs or trolling. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 4.69 pounds are excellent in 3- 8 feet of water on topwater frogs in the shoreline grass. Crappie are excellent with catches up to 13 inches on minnows and jigs on the main lake and scattered brush piles in 10-20 feet of water. White bass are slow to 1.50 pounds on crappie jigs and crankbaits in the lights at night or schooling in the open water of the main lake.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass continue to school in areas with lily pads and grass, so cast a frog for some topwater action.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: On the other hand, black bass and stripers have been slow, requiring extra patience from anglers targeting them.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: After the recent rise in lake level bass are spread out, with some moving into flooded brush. Largemouth bass are best early morning with small topwaters, or tiny 1.0 crankbaits.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Channel and blue catfish are excellent off the bank, while crappie, white bass, and black drum are all reporting good action, also with strong opportunities from the bank.
reports.by: Manny Martinez, Fishing With Manny

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: This lake typically boasts an abundance of largemouth bass and channel catfish.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early and late along the edges and can be found on offshore structures during the day. Crappie are holding on timber and structure in 12-20 feet, with many around 9.5 inches being caught on minnows, hair jigs, or plastics, though you may need to move to stay on them. Hybrid and white bass are schooling on flats and drop-off edges in 15-21 feet, hitting slabs, spoons, and shad - use the Outdoor Annual app to check the tooth patch and tell hybrids from whites.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie will start staging in deep water or creeks and river channels. Crappie are good in timber, brush and around docks with jigs or minnows.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie will start to roam and pull off structure. Crappie are good in timber, brush and around docks with jigs or minnows.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: The cooler weather should bring fish shallow and turn on the topwater bass bite. Bass are good early in the morning working underspins on points just off the grass, then rattle traps and deep diving crankbaits off the bank.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with topwaters early in the morning around grass or pond weed. Bass are schooling in creeks, so a hard-bodied popper should work. Lake Fork crappie fishing is heating back up as we begin to head into early fall. The black crappie are stacking up in huge numbers this week on brush piles and other structures. The white crappie are also showing up on timber along creek channels in 18-28 feet.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Mitchell's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles and docks in 12-15 feet of water on minnows.
reports.by: Big Country Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in standing timber near creek channels with minnows. Bass are feeding early and late on schooling shad in shallow water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie action continues to be good with many folks catching limits on many areas of the lake. Crappie are suspended near standing structure and near bridge pilings and deeper docks. Largemouth bass are good early on top water near laydowns near creek entrances.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good in shallow main lake cover and up river around cover. Crappie are very good on jigs and minnows fished in 4-16 feet of water around cover.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are active in the mornings around riprap, cypress trees, and brush piles, biting on grubs, spinnerbaits, crankbaits, and especially pink “cream” worms, before moving to offshore points and structures later in the day where Texas-rigged worms and deep crankbaits are producing. Crappie are steady in Lucious Bayou and the East Fork, holding tight to structure in 10-16 feet of water and hitting minnows and small hand-tied jigs. White bass are fantastic, with strong action in the river - deep-diving crankbaits off treelines in the West Fork and trolling 25-foot divers with gold pet spoons and yellow feathers on the south end, while vertical jigging with Duck Tracker slabs and a…
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is tough, with some schoolers caught on topwater and swimbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water early and late in the day, with fish deeper midday. White bass are fair with small silver or white slabs. Crappie are good on jigs. Bass are good with shallow running crankbaits, lightweight Texas rigs, lightweight jigs, topwater in the morning and evenings.
reports.by: Cade Rudiger, local angler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught in less than two feet of water with topwaters. Keep your eyes peeled for surfacing bass and cast a lipless crankbait or topwater. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good with a white spinnerbaits in the mornings around shallow structure. Crappie bite has been fair in brush piles around 18 feet of water.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be targeted on structure with Carolina rigged worms. Look for schooling bass and cast topwaters. Crappie can be found on brush piles with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on lipless crankbaits, underspin swimbaits, and Texas rigged worms. Crappie are good suspended in timber in 25 feet with minnows.
reports.by: Hambone Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
