reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair on topwater poppers, small walking baits, and flukes. Crappie are excellent with smaller fish on brush and bigger fish isolated in small groups in timber or creeks above the powerlines.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: The summer pattern has returned, leaving bass in a bit of a funk and seemingly confused about whether to stay deep or move shallow, making the fall transition uncertain. Crappie populations remain strong, while catfish are running slow. Largemouth bass are fair on topwater poppers, small walking baits, and flukes. Crappie are excellent on the deep brush piles with 1/32 ounce crappie jig on a light line.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15 feet of water on brush piles in the morning and evening with jigs or minnows. Bigger crappie are on the bottom. Largemouth bass are slow with occasional catch while targeting other species.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow with few catches up to 9 pounds, but fish are primarily 3-5 pounds. Target bass with topwater frogs, spooks and small creature baits flipped in heavy cover. Crappie are fair around bigger trees suspended 8-12 feet down.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting minnows on deep brush piles and around boat docks.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent, throwing a dropshot worm or Carlina rigged around mainlake points. Crappie are slow to fair with a white 1/32 ounce crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to go strong under brushed-out docks. Largemouth are crushing topwater at first light, then shifting to shallow crankbaits around dock legs as the sun climbs.
reports.by: Captain Casey Armstrong, Hooked Up Outfitters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are becoming more active as the water cools, with the best action coming around submerged logs, weed edges, and other structure on spinnerbaits, plastic worms, chatterbaits, and crankbaits. Bluegill and sunfish remain slow, though some bites are coming on nightcrawlers under a bobber, while catfish and crappie are also sluggish but can be found near structure in 8-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Aric Brooks, Huntsville State Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair and also moving relating to brush piles in 12-15 feet of water. Crappie are showing up at the bridge columns.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are being caught on squarebill crankbaits and chatterbaits on docks.
reports.by: Terry Hawkins Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow at the marina, but bluegill remain fair with crickets and worms, and catfish remain good with minnows or punch bait. The crappie are fair with jigs or minnows over brush in 8-15 feet of water. Black bass are slow on crankbaits and soft plastic baits in 6-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair as fish transition to brush in the channels with live minnows or jigs.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Quality sized bass are good in 2-5 feet of water with soft plastics. Crappie are fair with fish scattered in mid depths and on brush on concrete structures.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Some smaller schoolie-sized largemouth bass are feeding on the surface on the lower third of the lake. A small, clear soft plastic on a jighead cast fast and accurately is about the only thing these shad-eating bass will respond to consistently.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Catfish are still producing well on trotlines and jug lines, while crappie are fair north of Highway 59.
reports.by: Chad Kinsfather, Lavaca Navidad River Authority

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Small swim baits or slabs are catching them. Largemouth and smallmouth bass can be found off the banks in 5-12 feet of water with a hard drop-off. Crappie fishing is about improve to good as water temperatures drop and shad schools are larger in the lake. Live bait is doing fair, or cast topwaters switching to slabs later in the day.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing on Lake Travis is still strong as water temperatures cool to the low 80s. Bass are following shad into the mouths of creeks and coves. Bass are also feeding on flats and shallow ledges around larger boulders.
reports.by: Tyler Torwick, Torwick's Guiding Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair as fish transition to brush in the channels with live minnows or jigs.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good on live bait and small artificials 1/16-1/32 ounce in 10-18 feet of water on brush or structure. Black bass are good on a wacky worm or crankbaits. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are up in the main lake in brush 15-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass are good using soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent in shallow water up against cattails and and any structure using shallow water crankbaits and spinnerbaits. Crappie are slow, but can be caught off docks with live bait.
reports.by: Michael James, local angler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20-35 feet on minnows fishing over trees.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair in the bays chasing shad.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good and can be caught on the outside of grass lines with Texas rig worms and weightless flukes. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to concentrate around bridges.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the discharge with swimbaits, worms or a shaky head. Grass edges and reed edges are loaded up with bass, so cast a fluke, shad shaped swimbait, or a frog or wakebait. Bass can be caught on deep points and humps, or shallow by the reeds. The bass size tends to be larger and more active later in the day.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: This active tactic with MAL Lures is easily outfishing slabs snap jigged off bottom.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in 10-20 feet on brush piles with jigs or minnows. Windy banks and main lake points should produce strikes from bass. Spotted and black bass are fair but can consistently be caught with 3-4 inch shad swimbaits on secondary points with grass or timber.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with frogs over pond weed early in the morning on cloudy days.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Slabs will put fish in the boat. Largemouth bass are good on topwater baits on main lake points and swimbaits later in the day. Crappie are still good on minnows around docks and mid depth brush piles.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 6 pounds are excellent on frogs and swimbaits in the grass and weeds, or on crankbaits off the rocks in 2-8 feet around the rock cuts. Crappie are fair with catches up to 10 inches around docks with brush on minnows in 15-18 feet and some offshore brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on brush piles and standing timber in 20-25 feet of water with chartreuse jigs and minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Look for bass in rock piles in 5-15 feet of water and bang a crankbait around them for some good bites.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Some bass are being caught around reed lines.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Good stacks of hybrids and white bass are being found on midlake points and drop offs along sandy flats throughout the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch and the spillway humps in 11-17 feet. Cast spinners and slabs and look for schooling fish on these flats as well as deeper seawalls and shorelines. Use spinnerbaits or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. Cast rattletraps, spoons, umbrella rigs, slabs or sassy shads to get the hybrids to bite. The crappie bite has been getting better. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in 5-12 feet…
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass to 8 pounds are good on a variety of soft plastics including dropshot rigs. Anglers are boasting about catching 40-70 bass per day.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water early and late in the day, then seeking deeper structure and shaded docks midday. Crappie have been fair with some decent catches, but you have to move frequently sifting thought the bream in 8-25 feet of water. Many folks are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, others are using slabs from Bradley Outdoors to jig for them.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Corpus Christi Lake fishing report
reports.text: Boat anglers reported catches of crappie in 15-20 feet, a few smaller sized catfish and little gar.
reports.by: Weber’s Boat Landing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in 10-20 feet on brush piles with jigs or minnows. Spotted and black bass are fair but can consistently be caught with 3-4 inch shad swimbaits on secondary points with grass or timber.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good shallow early in the morning with a rattle trap. Topwater action for bass is spotty.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on topwaters early in the morning around grass. Streamers are tempting active feeding bass in 1-3 feet on main lake points. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork is just phenomenal right now going into the early winter months. You can find crappie almost everywhere on the lake but if you find the right area they are loaded up. We are seeing some black crappie grouped up in numbers. The huge white crappie has been showing off the past month also.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding up on shad all over the lake. Bass are good on moving baits like spinnerbaits and crankbaits. Crappie are on brush about 13-15 feet deep on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Striped bass are slow to fair with catches up to 10 pounds on slabs and live shad fished on the lower ends. Largemouth bass to 7 pounds are possible on crankbaits and soft plastics fished on shallow humps near creek channels. Some good reports of largemouth bass in the river north of Hunter Park on laydowns. Crappie action continues to be good on flooded timber and bridge pilings on small jigs and minnows. Some good crappie catches have been reported from near Water’s Edge to the timber by the Peninsula.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are shallow in the morning feeding heavily in worms and grubs. Crappie are great in the rivers being caught on small jigs tight to structure in 12-16 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be caught on brush with minnows and jigs. Bass can be caught on topwater early and late in the day.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is pretty tough, but fish are moving shallower.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught on structures in 3-8 feet of water with soft plastics. Crappie are shallow in creek channels or ditches with wood in 5 feet of water.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Spotted and black bass are fair but can consistently be caught with 3-4 inch shad swimbaits on secondary points with grass or timber. Crappie are great on timber in 10-25 feet of water.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 6-14 feet this week. Largemouth bass are good in 2-14 feet of water on brush piles, rocks and docks using moving baits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good early morning and late afternoon fishing points and the edge of hydrilla with crazy shad topwater baits and Texas rigged redbug worms. Crappie are good but getting harder to find on brush piles and laydowns in 18-30 feet.
reports.by: Hambone Guide service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent with an abundance of 2-4 pound fish schooling in 12-15 feet. Crappie are good with numbers of keepers being caught on white jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are good with catches 2-5 pounds with green pumpkins dropshots. Crappie are fair for keeper sized fish biting white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been fair on white chatterbaits and spinnerbaits early morning and evening. Midday flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water is the ticket to catch shaded up largemouth bass. Crappie were good around boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass up to 7.75 pounds can be caught near the marina dock. Crappie are hit-or-miss with some big fish being caught.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass continue to be slow with catches up to 6 pounds possible. A lot of bass are chasing dragonflies in shallow water being caught on frogs and topwaters, and chatterbaits. Crappie slow and scattered, but can be caught suspended 8 feet down on timber with minnows or white/chartresue jigs.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The white bass are being caught using small spoons such as the Bomber slab. A few reports of crappie being caught on brush piles with BoneHead jigs.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow with only a few catches to report. Crappie are slow on minnows.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with small swimbaits and natural colored deep diving crankbaits. Crappie are good on standing timber in 10-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are slow in 20-30 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs or rattle traps. Bass are slow in 5-15 feet of water on ledges and points with chatterbaits, small crankbaits, and plastics. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: White bass can be caught on points and humps in 15-25 feet on live bait and slabs. Crappie are good in 5-20 feet on brush piles and small patches of structure, minnows.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fall pattern is fair good on brush piles in 10-15 feet of water.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is slow, bluegill and catfish are fair. Crappie are fair over brush in 8-16 feet of water with jigs and minnows. Black bass are slow moving plastics in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing has been hit-or-miss with fish reorienting from hydrilla to the lake's sparse natural cover.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is picking up with cooler temperatures and potential inflow if we get rain. Crappie action will increase with cooler temperatures as fish move up and hold tight to brush and around creeks. Striped bass are best on topwaters early in the morning, then switch to slabs on shallow flats in 12-25 feet of water with topwaters and slabs.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: First few hours of the morning are producing bass on the lower end in the grass. Bass are good with 3-4 pound catches coming in the river and backs of coves on rocky points with crankbaits and topwaters. There is a good topwater bass bite due to the cooler morning temperatures. Bass are also feeding around the grass, so cast a Texas-rigged soft plastic like a worm, craw or jig.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow with some decent size fish suspended in 16-20 feet of water with minnows. Bass are fair on topwater baits, crankbaits and spinnerbaits scattered throughout the lake. Crappie are good scattered on docks in 6-8 feet of water, or on the southern end of the lake chasing shad on minnows.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Fall conditions are in effect and bass are still chasing shad so they can be caught with multiple moving techniques like swimbaits, spinnerbaits, crankbaits and jerkbaits off the reed lines and in the open flats and points. Bass also keying in on dragonflies which means they’re still hitting top water some, but that bite seems to be slowing down overall.
reports.by: Team YAKUSA

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20-35 feet on shad colored jigs and minnows fishing over trees.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair in the shallows, 2-5 feet on frogs, buzzbaits, flukes, top waters squarebill crankbaits.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be caught with live bait.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good and can be caught on outside grass lines with Texas rig worms and weightless flukes. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: There is lots of grass up on the north end for bass to relate to. Flukes and senko type baits will catch keeper bass.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good working soft jerkbaits like flukes and shallow crankbaits along reeds and grass edges close to and around points and partly into coves and cuts. Bass can be caught on senkos in the grass, with some keepers and many undersized fish.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: The MAL Original used by cranking it up off the bottom about 6-7 times is outproducing slabs while the white bass and shad are both moving far and fast in this temperature of water.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in 10-20 feet on brush piles with jigs or minnows. Windy banks and main lake points should produce strikes from bass. Spotted bass are still schooling at the dam, and can be caught in high numbers with an underspin or 4 inch shad swimbait. Largemouth bass catches are excellent when casting a spinnerbait or bladed jig on wind-blown points, especially points with grass. White bass and largemouth can still be caught around green lights at night on small profile shad baits.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass bite has slowed down but bass can be caught covering lots of pond weed with Ribbetts.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass and hybrids have been good on slabs. Crappie continue to be great on minnows and jigs on docks and offshore brush piles. Try a noisy topwater before daylight on main lake points and the face of the dam for largemouth bass.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair with catches up to 4.67 pounds on topwater frogs and swimbaits in the grass and weeds, or with crankbaits off rocks cuts in 2-8 feet. Crappie are fair to 10 inches around docks with brush on minnows in 12-15 feet and some offshore brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles and standing timber in 20-25 feet of water with chartreuse jigs and minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Look for bass in rock piles in 5-15 feet of water and bang a crankbait around them for some good bites.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are still in transition while the daily temperature is still in the upper 80s.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Topwater lures are productive for bass in the morning, then as the sun rises drag a dropshot on the grass edges.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are dispersed throughout the lake relating primarily near stumps and boat houses. Crappie are slow with jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are excellent with catches up to 8 pounds on soft plastics and crankbaits with many anglers boasting 50 plus fish a day.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass good cranking rocks and flipping docks. Crappie have been slow in 12-22 feet with hair jigs producing more strikes than plastics. Many folks are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, or jigging with slabs from Bradley Outdoors, as well as casting swimbaits or crankbaits.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in 10-20 feet on brush piles with jigs or minnows. High numbers of small bass can be caught around reeds or emergent vegetation on a white buzzbait, or Texas rigged fluke at daybreak.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on topwaters early around grass, and lipless crankbaits in front of the grass and in the flats 3-6 feet. Streamers are tempting active feeding bass in 1-3 feet on main lake points. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork is improving as the water temperature drop into the 70s.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good to excellent on many areas of the lake on slabs and spinnerbaits. Largemouth bass are good in numbers with some good fish to 7 pounds possible. Largemouth bass are good on crankbaits and soft plastics fished in the back of sloughs near docks and near main lake points. Crappie are excellent on small jigs and minnows fished on structure from Indian Harbor to Bentwater.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good with catches up to 5 pounds on plastic worms. Crappie are good in 4-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Birds are working along the north and south shorelines. moving quickly so double rigged with a slab and jig.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Streamers fished above grass and near lilies should draw bass.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are starting to hit large swimbaits along with worms and grubs on the shallow structure. Crappie are decent in the upper channels eating minnows and small jig heads tight to structure.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Smaller fish are biting topwaters, and bigger fish were caught on square bill crankbaits for jerkbaits for schooling bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: The best bass bite has been with fishing worms, Texas rig or shaky head off of boat docks and brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass good early and late. Look for schools of bait around shallow cover in 3-6 feet and you’ll find bass. Crappie mid depth on minnows.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught with shad colored bladed jigs along grass lines, and flipping shallow cover around the mouths of coves can produce bites. Crappie are great on timber in 10-25 feet of water.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great with 1/32-1/8 ounce jigs or minnows. Black bass are on fire fishing early mornings in 3-20 feet with the bigger sized catches in 7-15 feet with spinnerbaits. Then gradually go to a 12-15 foot diver, Texas rig or Carolina rig as the sun rises higher around 10 a.m. but, if you are still able to catch bass with a squarebill crankbait, do not switch to the 12 foot diver until you have covered at least two places that you normally catch bass at. There are some 3-5 pound bass shallow in 2-5 feet of water feeding on bundles of gizzard shad and threadfin shad. Black bass set up in 4-7 feet of water on single boulders or stumps to ambush the shad. Do not be surprised if you catch…
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on chartreuse jigs and minnows in 12-20 feet of water on brush. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, jigs, and live bait are working. Crappie are fair in 6-26 feet of water. Bass are best early morning or at sunset hitting jigs, spinnerbaits and crankbaits. Bass are cruising shallow cover eating shad or bluegill. Crappie are on deeper brush piles in 12-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 4-12 feet with some suspended 16 feet down. Largemouth bass are in 2-14 feet of water on brush piles, rocks and docks using moving baits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good using shaky heads and Texas rigged worms on main points with hydrilla. Crappie are good suspended in deep brush piles but are beginning to scatter heading towards the warmer water.
reports.by: Hambone Guide service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millers Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Very few catches of crappie in 20 feet of water. Bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent with an abundance of 2-5 pound fish schooling in 12-15 feet. Crappie are excellent with numbers of keepers being caught on white and chartreuse 1/16 ounce jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are good with catches in the 2-4 pound range. Crappie are excellent with small 1/16 ounce white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are undersized off the docks and scattered throughout the lake hitting primarily larger minnows. Largemouth bass are good throughout the lake, with many undersized or babies everywhere.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow to 7 pounds. Bass are starting to bite flipping creature baits like a Hags Cheat Code in green pumpkin or in Ramsey Revenge, and chatterbaits like a Hags Hurricane in white or chartreuse/white up the river. Crappie are slow around pecan trees but you will have to fish multiple trees with minnows to get a good mess of fish.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The white bass are being caught using small spoons such as the Bomber slab. A few reports of crappie being caught on brush piles with BoneHead jigs. Reports of an 8 pound and 9 pound bass caught.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Cooler weather has improved the fishing, especially for bass and hybrids, and the thermoclines continue to move deeper. Bass are good, especially early and late in the day the bass have been feeding more predictably, closer to shoreline points, reeds and windblown current areas near bridges.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in deep water around brush piles with minnows. Black bass are slow.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with small swimbaits and dropshots in 2-12 feet of water. Crappie are fair on white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are still slow in 20-30 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs or rattle traps. Report by TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service.Bass are scattered on deep brush and ledges hitting deep diving crankbaits, Carolina rigs, and jigs. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service.Bass are scattered on deep brush and ledges…

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: The fall crappie brush pile bite is fair to good in 10-15 feet of water on minnows.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Shallow bass feeding on the shad can be caught with spinnerbaits and topwater frogs. Crappie are transitioning from brush main lake brush to creek channels. Shallow bass are centered around shoreline brush and hay grass along with high spots, shallow ditches and creek channel swings. There is a large population of schooling bass heavily chasing bait balls around main lake ledges in 17-22 feet, main lake drains in 10-17 feet, and main lake and secondary points.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is slow, bluegill and catfish are fair. Crappie are slow over brush in 8-16 feet of water with jigs and minnows. Black bass are fair on slow moving plastics in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: The reports are very slow for black bass.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass anglers report hit-or-miss fishing, especially around sunrise and sunset. After the loss of the hydrilla crop on the lake during the flooding in May, bass have relocated to sparse natural cover.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing will pick up as water temperatures drop and fish move towards the brush and creeks in 10-15 feet of water. Bass fishing is slow as water levels remain below average, exposing shorelines. Striped bass are good on shallow flats in 12-25 feet of water with topwaters and slabs.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has improved with catches up to 9 pounds this week. Bass are shallow in 1-5 feet of water on topwater lures, swimbaits and chatterbaits during the first couple of hours. Few more crappie getting caught this week on shallow brush and at night on lighted deeper docks.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: First few hours of the morning are producing bass on the lower end in the grass. Bass are good with 3-4 pound catches coming in the river and backs of coves on rocky points with crankbaits and topwaters. Quite a few bass are shallow around the new cover. Bass fishing on Lake Travis is really picking up.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with minnows and jigs in 16-20 feet of water on brush. Bass are fair on topwater baits, crankbaits and spinnerbaits scattered throughout the lake.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair with some keepers being caught in 10-12 feet of water on brush piles with jigs. Bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Welsh fishing report
reports.text: A few reports that catches of bass are good.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass can be caught off the shore with soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair, on chunk rock points, ledges, steep bluffs with Pop Rs, Zara Puppy, swim jigs, weightless senkos, wacky rigs, Ned rigs, and weightless flukes.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been picking up with the cooler temperatures and less boat traffic on the lake.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in 15-20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows or jigs. Black bass are chasing shad and bream. Windy retaining walls will produce marauding bass. Bass can be caught throwing a white buzzbait in the early morning around hard cover will produce bites.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is hot with fish on timber, brush or any structure you can find in 8-25 feet of water. This is definitely a lake to hit up if you are looking for a mess of crappie.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Some bass are being caught in weeds and should get better with cooler weather on the way.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Sand Bass and hybrids have been good on slabs near the main lake structure. Largemouth bass have been good early on topwaters like spooks and buzzbaits. Crappie continue to be good on minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Some white bass are starting to show up in the river systems and you still have the black bass feeding on shad in the grass and pads. Look for the bait on your graph or look for the birds, remember to listen for the pads popping as that is bait under them and the bass will be there.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on shad colored crankbait, or green pumpkin soft plastics. Crappie are biting on deep brush in 25 feet of water with live minnows or black and chartreuse grubs.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and catfish are biting well on minnows and cut bait. No reports on bass this week.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to boast numbers of largemouth bass a day on soft plastics and crankbaits.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to poor on brush 10-22 feet on minnows and hand tied jigs. Lots of big bream on brush with the crappie can be caught on minnows and worms. Bass still holding true to shallow early and offshore docks midday. Many folks are trolling with a deep diver and a pet spoon trailer, others are using slabs from Bradley Outdoors to jig for them as well as casting swimbaits or crankbaits.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 10-15 feet of water on minnows. High numbers of small bass can be caught around reeds or emergent vegetation on a white buzzbait, or Texas rigged fluke at daybreak.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water early in the morning with rattle traps. After the morning bite bass can be caught in 12-15 feet of water with shaky heads.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass topwaters are good early around grass after sun up and mid range in 4-6 feet square bills on flats with grass and timber lines. Windy banks can provide schooling bass action, so be ready with a small topwater lure or streamer. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork is improving as the water temperature drop into the 70s.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on topwater baits in the morning and evening. Crappie are on brush piles good on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in numbers with an occasional fish to 6 pounds possible. Crappie continue to be good mid-lake on submerged timber.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good up the river on crankbaits, worms, and spinnerbaits. Crappie are very good to 2 pounds on minnows and jigs fished 5 feet down over brush piles. White bass are good on slab spoons fished in 10-18 feet of water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good moving quickly so double rigged with a slab and jig.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are great on worms and grubs in 4-8 feet of water in the east and west fork. Crappie are plentiful in the east fork and the mouths of Luces Bayou holding tight to structure in 8-14 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie over brush piles.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass schooling activity can be seen on the surface near main creek channels, and a weightless fluke is hard to beat.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great with 1/32-1/8 ounce jigs or minnows. Black bass are in 3-20 feet with the bigger sized catches in 7-15 feet. Then gradually go to a 12-15 foot diver, Texas rig or Carolina rig as the sun rises higher around 10 a.m. but, if you are still able to catch bass with a squarebill crankbait, do not switch to the 12 foot diver until you have covered at least two places that you normally catch bass at. There are some 3-5 pound bass shallow in 2-5 feet of water. all day long because there are some shallow right now. The black bass are usually in about 4-7 feet of water on the outside of the black bands of shad, set up on some kind of ambush points such as just one single boulder or…
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, jigs, and live bait are working. Crappie are fair in 60-26 feet of water. Bass are more active at night. Largemouth bass are slow on jigs and finesse worms. Crappie are heavily stacking up in main lake brush piles in 12-15 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on redbug colored texas rigged worms fishing points with hydrilla. Crappie remain good with fish suspended 15 feet over brush using minnows and Bobby Garland screamer color jigs.
reports.by: Hambone guide service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent for numbers with fish in the 2-4 pound range biting Carolina rigs and medium diving crankbaits. Crappie are excellent on brush piles and standing timber from 10-15 feet of water with white and chartreuse 1/16 ounce jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass will bite squarebill crankbaits in 5 feet, if you find them hugging the bottom in 8-10 feet dragging a Texas-rig Mag-worm can be effective. Crappie population is good. Bass are good with lots of topwater activity and schooling action. Bass between the 2-4 pound range on topwaters, walking baits, spooks and poppers. Crappie are excellent with catches of very large crappie.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow, but good numbers can be caught on frogs and whopper ploppers very shallow. A few Bass up to 6 pounds reported near the dam on Alabama rigs suspended over open water. Crappie are good on a variety of jigs but the best color has been red with white skirt or small shad imitation jigs, or minnows.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on minnows or jigs. Black bass are not biting at all.
reports.by: David Holt, Lake Palo Pinto RV Park and Resort

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair with some schooling action biting small swimbaits and topwaters. Crappie are slow on crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are still slow in 20-30 feet of water with live shad or small slabs and jigs or rattle traps. Bass are scattered on ledges, points, and deep timber hitting crankbaits, Carolina rigs, dropshots. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with flukes, worms, and lipless crankbaits near the hydrilla grass edge are reported to be working for bass. No angler reports of crappie or catfish this week, but anglers can try minnows on crappie jigs near brush piles or piers to target crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Slabs and Mepps spinners are best when schools are located off main lake points. The fall crappie brush pile bite in 10-15 feet of water appears to be starting. October is normally a very good month for crappie.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are fair in shallow cattails.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Hybrid stripers and white bass have been solid on slabs, slab-spinners and swimbaits. The largemouth bite has been good.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Catfish are good all over and bass are good north of U.S.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie remain tough, sticking to brush and structure in 12-18 feet of water. Bass fishing remains slow, however, as water temperatures cool, bass are moving up. When the topwater bite ends cast swimbaits into the shallows for box fish, then switch to slabs later in the morning.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are still slow at this time.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on topwater in the marinas, and lower end grass. Midday crankbaits are landing bass midlake.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good. We should expect a lot more bass in hydrilla going forward.
reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with small sized fish being caught off of ledges and main lake points with minnows and jigs. Bass are slow on deeper water ledges with crankbaits and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 15-30 feet on jigs and minnows fishing over trees.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on main and secondary points, ledges and suspended in 15-25 feet.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass can typically be caught early in the discharge with baitfish colored small swimbaits, flukes, crankbaits and clear topwaters. Work all points and along the dam using crankbaits or small ball head jigs with small straight tail swimbaits to catch bass.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite is fair around grass or pond weed with ribbets and horny toads over grass. Crappie fishing is hot with fish on timber, brush or any structure you can find in 8-25 feet of water. This is definitely a lake to hit up if you are looking for a mess of crappie.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Slabs and live bait have been effective. Crappie fishing continues to be on fire! Largemouth bass have been excellent on topwaters at sunrise.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 5.67 pounds are fair on frogs in the grass and weeds. Crappie are fair with catches up to 10 inches caught near docks with brush on minnows in 12-15 feet and some offshore brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles and standing timber in 25 feet of water with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good working rock piles with crankbaits and swimbaits to catch active Fish.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Blue catfish are being caught on the road bed in front of the crappie wall on cut bait.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Good stacks of hybrids and white bass are being found on midlake points and drop offs along sandy flats throughout the dam area, Crappie Island, Key Ranch and the spillway humps in 11-17 feet. Cast spinners and slabs and look for schooling fish on these flats as well as deeper seawalls and shorelines. Use spinnerbaits or drop a slab down to the bottom and work it fast up and down and the fish will hit it immediately. Also throwing out a slab and reeling it back with a slow retrieve is also working well. Cast rattle traps, Spoons, Umbrella Rigs, slabs or sassy shads to get the hybrids to bite. The crappie bite has been getting better. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in 5-12 feet…
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Bass are hitting topwaters. Crappie are hitting on minnows, or pretty much any kind of bait you can buy from the bait shop there biting on like crazy this week.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Anglers have not been disappointed with daily limits of largemouth bass up to 8 pounds and eater sized channel catfish are common. Many largemouth bass anglers were boasting on 50-100 fish days.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are poor to fair in 14-21 feet with a few folks able to find some but the population is still low and will be for the next couple years most likely. Bass have been good chasing bait shallow early and moving offshore and under docks as the relentless sun gets higher in the sky.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 10-15 feet of water on minnows. Bass are on hard cover, and can be caught with a dropshot or shaky head worm.
reports.by: Joey Crews, Lake Bob Sandlin Chubby Chaser Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in brush piles with crankbaits and soft plastics. No reports on crappie.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water early in the morning with rattle traps. After the morning bite bass can be caught in 12 feet of water with shaky heads and Carolina rigs.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early on top waters and frogs and flukes near pond weed. Windy banks can provide schooling bass action, so be ready with a small topwater lure or streamer. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork is improving as the water temperature drop into the 70s.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are reporting good catches of crappie. Largemouth bass are good on topwaters along the rocks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are feeding on shad, so there is a good bite casting topwater in the morning and evening. Crappie are on brush piles biting minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie action continues to be fair to good on jigs and small minnows fished near underwater structures in 10-15 feet of water. Largemouth bass to 6 pounds are possible working creek entrances and docks from Decordova to Indian Harbor. Some good largemouth catches are reported in the river near Tin Top.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good with catches up to 5 pounds on crankbaits and worms fished in timber up river. Crappie are very good on jigs and minnows fished over cover in 4-12 feet of water. White bass are good on slab spoons fishing over humps and roadbeds.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good double rigged with a slab and jig.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are eating very well off points and mouths of waterways being caught on crankbaits, grubs and worms. Crappie are tight to structure, chewing on hand tied jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: There has been a lot of sporadic schooling for white bass and largemouth bass. Crappie can be caught on minnows under the bridges.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught on creek channel bends throwing Texas rigged creature baits, senkos, or compact jigs in black and blue. Crappie are starting to migrate to creek channels timber in 6-30 feet of water with jigs.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are great with 1/32-1/8 ounce jigs or minnows. Black bass are in 3-20 feet, with bigger fish being caught in 7-15 feet. Do not be surprised if you catch crappie or catfish, while trying to catch the bluegills. Lunker bass patrol the piles too. Crappie are starting to migrate to creek channels timber in 15 feet of water with minnows.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20 feet of water over brush piles with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are slow with some topwater action early in the morning. Limits of bass can be caught near Main lake docks, and docks in The Colorado River with white swimbait and white chatterbaits, following up with a shaky head craw and baby brush hogs.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass can be caught in 14 feet of water. Crappie are good in 8-14 feet of water with minnows or jigs.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: The midday bite is in 10-20 feet of water with Duck Tracker slabs.
reports.by: Michael Richardson, Lake Livingston Adventures

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good early and late fishing the hydrilla with pop R’s, spinnerbaits and Texas rigged worms. Crappie are good fishing brush piles and timber in 20-25 feet with fish suspended at 15 feet.
reports.by: Hambone guide service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent with 3-5 pound fish being caught on Carolina rig, dropshot and deep crankbaits. Crappie are fair on 1/8 ounce white crappie jig on a split shot.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass will bite squarebill crankbaits in 5 feet, if you find them hugging the bottom in 8-10 feet dragging a Texas-rig Mag-worm can be effective. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent on dropshots, small paddle tail swimbaits in 4-12 feet of water. Crappie are excellent on brush and standing timber in 10-15 feet of water on 1/16 ounce white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow to 5 pounds on frogs, Whopper floppers and chatterbaits. Crappie are fair suspended in trees, or suspended in 10-15 feet of water in deep water. Minnows are still best but some fish are caught on red and white or blue and white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass bite is improving with reports of fishing being caught on swimbaits. A report of an 8 pound bass being caught on a Seek & Destroy Glide bait. Crappie are good with reports of fish stacked up.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been slow, except during the cooler weather periods, but remain primarily on boathouse patterns. White bass and hybrid stripers remain good early and late, with live minnows, trolled spoons, and casting a Little George lure and small slabs.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite has slowed. Bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on small paddle tail swimbaits in 4-12 feet of water. Crappie are good on brush piles and standing timber using 1/8 ounce white translucent crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are slow in 20-30 feet of water using live shad or small white and silver slabs and jigs or rattle traps. Bass are scattered on ledges, points, and deep timber hitting crankbaits, Carolina rigs, dropshots. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Later in the morning sand bass move to 16-28 feet of water on humps, levees and long points using 3/4 ounce slabs. Crappie are fair and relating to brush in 15-22 feet deep and suspended on bridge pylons moving on and off structure on minnows.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 5-20 feet with minnows out fishing jigs. Some can be caught off points on live bait and slabs.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Slabs and Mepps spinners are best when schools are located off main lake points. October is usually an awesome month for crappie as the water temperature cools.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling more in the morning so expect more topwater action on grass edges and points. Crappie are fair on standing timber in 27 feet on brush piles with minnows over jigs. Shallow bass are centered around shoreline brush and hay grass along with high spots, shallow ditches and creek channel swings. There is a large population of schooling bass heavily chasing bait balls around main lake ledges in 17-22 feet, main lake drains in 10-17 feet, and main lake and secondary points.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are reporting success on smaller bass in the shallows.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on soft plastics. Crappie are fair on concrete.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: This has produced some visible, fishable topwater action on the lower third of Stillhouse with a mixture of largemouth bass and white bass pinning threadfin shad against the surface.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Seems like fish are preferring slabs and in-line spinners over swimbaits. The crappie bite is turning on in 6-12 feet ok brush piles with minnows. Largemouth bass are good early on square bills near rip rap.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in the main lake at 14-20 feet, but most are still small to just keepers, these fish coming on big crankbaits and Carolina rigs. Crappie are still slow.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling in the marinas throughout the day hitting topwater and swimbaits.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow and small, with undersized fish scattered in 7-15 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good on worms, frogs, and topwaters. Bass and hybrids have been schooling on and off all day long. Crappie are good in the grass. reports.by: David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair with small sized fish being caught on deep brush piles with minnows and jigs. Bass are slow on deeper water ledges with crankbaits and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in 15-25 feet on jigs and minnows fishing over trees.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair in 15-25 feet on ledges, chunk rock points off the Rio Grande.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with creature baits or craws near dock pylons.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in 15-20 feet of water on brush piles with minnows or jigs. Black bass are chasing shad and bream. Windy retaining walls will produce marauding bass.
